- added comparison by ref to blob dict

## Walkthrough

This pull request modifies internal logic in two packages. In blob-dictionary.ts, the root-level subkey construction changes from using a subarray to the full key, path traversal order is reordered, and lookup matching is broadened to support both exact object reference and value-based equality checks. In disputes.ts, validator key collection construction is refactored from a filter-based array approach to a HashSet-based approach with direct key removal. Both changes are internal logic modifications with no public API alterations.

<details>
<summary>packages/core/collections/blob-dictionary.ts (2)</summary><blockquote>

`194-194`: **LGTM! Good allocation avoidance at depth 0.**

When `depth === 0`, `key.raw.subarray(0)` returns a view of the entire array. Using `key` directly avoids the unnecessary `BytesBlob.blobFrom()` allocation while maintaining semantic equivalence. This aligns with the CODESTYLE.md guidance on avoiding unnecessary allocations.

---

`421-428`: **Reference comparison optimization is safe but may have limited effectiveness.**

The added `item[0] === key` check is a valid micro-optimization—reference comparison is O(1) versus byte-by-byte comparison in `isEqualTo`. However, since `internalSet` creates a new `BytesBlob` via `BytesBlob.blobFrom(key.raw.subarray(...))` at line 122, the stored `SubKey` will be a different object from the lookup key in typical insert-then-get flows.

The optimization would primarily benefit scenarios where the same object reference is used across multiple operations. Since the fallback to `isEqualTo` ensures correctness and the reference check is cheap, this is harmless—just worth noting the limited benefit in standard usage patterns. Based on CODESTYLE.md, micro-optimizations should be measured and verified.




Consider whether there's a measurable performance improvement. If not, this could be simplified to just `isEqualTo`.

</blockquote></details>
<details>
<summary>packages/jam/transition/disputes/disputes.ts (1)</summary><blockquote>

`408-419`: **LGTM! Good optimization iterating over the smaller collection.**

The PR's stated goal of "reversed a loop to iterate over the smaller collection" is achieved here. Instead of filtering all validator keys against the punish set, you now:
1. Build a `HashSet` of all validator keys
2. Iterate over `punishSetKeys` (typically smaller) and delete each

This is more efficient when `punishSet.size << validatorCount`, as `HashSet.delete` is O(1) amortized. The `delete` method safely handles non-existent keys by returning `false` without throwing, so correctness is preserved.

</blockquote></details>

</blockquote></details>

</details>
